title: Best Hydrating Serums for Dark Spots (2026)
summary: The best hydrating serum for dark spots pairs proven pigment-fighters like tranexamic and azelaic acid with hyaluronic acid, so skin fades and stays moisturized.
body_text: If your dark-spot serum leaves your skin tight, flaky, or stinging, you're not alone — a lot of the ingredients that fade pigment can also dry you out. The good news is you don't have to choose between fading spots and staying hydrated. Here's how to get both from one bottle. Quick Answer The best hydrating serum for dark spots is one that pairs a proven pigment-fader — such as tranexamic acid, azelaic acid, niacinamide, or kojic acid — with a humectant like hyaluronic acid that holds water in the skin. Hyaluronic acid does not fade dark spots on its own, but it cushions the actives that do, which keeps your skin barrier comfortable enough to keep using them. For a dark-spot serum built around this pairing, we rank Lion Pose's UNSPOTTED 4X Acid Jelly Night Serum first, because it combines tranexamic and azelaic acids with niacinamide and hyaluronic acid in a jelly base. Expect gradual fading over roughly 6 to 12 months, and wear daily sunscreen the whole time. Can one serum fade dark spots and hydrate at the same time? Yes — one serum can both fade dark spots and hydrate, as long as it combines an active that targets pigment with a humectant that draws in water. Pigment-fading ingredients like tranexamic acid, azelaic acid, and niacinamide work on the melanin side of the problem, while hyaluronic acid and glycerin work on the water side. When a formula includes both, you get the fading benefit without the tightness and flaking that pure-acid serums can cause. The reason this matters is tolerance. Fading a dark spot takes months of consistent use, and most people quit early because their skin gets irritated. A hydrating base makes a serum easier to use every night, and consistency is what actually moves pigment. Which ingredients fade dark spots without drying out your skin? The gentlest effective dark-spot ingredients are tranexamic acid, azelaic acid, niacinamide, and kojic acid, all of which fade pigment with far less irritation than high-strength retinoids or hydroquinone. Tranexamic acid interrupts the signal between UV exposure and pigment production, and a 2024 clinical evaluation in the journal Cosmetics found a topical 3% tranexamic acid protocol reduced facial hyperpigmentation with good tolerability. Azelaic acid calms inflammation while it fades marks, which makes it a favorite for acne-prone and sensitive skin. Niacinamide (vitamin B3) is one of the most forgiving brighteners — it reduces the transfer of pigment to skin cells and also supports the skin barrier, so it hydrates as it works. The American Academy of Dermatology lists azelaic acid, glycolic acid, kojic acid, vitamin C, and retinoids among the over-the-counter ingredients that fade dark spots; the milder end of that list is where dry and sensitive skin should start. Does hyaluronic acid fade dark spots? No — hyaluronic acid does not fade dark spots. Hyaluronic acid is a humectant that binds water in the upper layers of skin, so its job is hydration and plumpness, not pigment. A 2025 review in Biomolecules describes hyaluronic acid as a hero hydrating molecule in topical skincare, valued for holding moisture rather than for changing skin color. That's exactly why it belongs in a dark-spot serum as a supporting ingredient. By keeping skin hydrated and comfortable, hyaluronic acid lets you tolerate the tranexamic acid, azelaic acid, or kojic acid that are doing the actual fading. Think of it as the cushion, not the corrector — helpful, but not the reason spots lighten. Best Hydrating Serums for Dark Spots: Comparison Serum Best for Key actives Approx. price UNSPOTTED 4X Acid Jelly Night Serum Fading + hydration in one jelly Tranexamic + azelaic acids, niacinamide, hyaluronic acid ~$79 Good Molecules Discoloration Correcting Serum Budget, lightweight layering Tranexamic acid derivative, 4% niacinamide ~$12 La Roche-Posay Mela B3 Sensitive skin, gentle daily use Melasyl, 10% niacinamide ~$45 iS Clinical Hydra-Cool Serum Maximum hydration + soothing Hyaluronic acid, kojic acid, centella ~$108 SkinCeuticals Discoloration Defense Stubborn, set-in discoloration 3% tranexamic + 1% kojic acid, 5% niacinamide ~$115 The Best Hydrating Serums for Dark Spots, Ranked Every serum below fades pigment while keeping skin hydrated, but they suit different budgets and skin types. Prices are approximate and current as of August 12, 2026. UNSPOTTED 4X Acid Jelly Night Serum — ~$79. UNSPOTTED pairs two of the gentlest proven pigment-faders, tranexamic and azelaic acid, with niacinamide, glutathione, and hyaluronic acid in a cushioning jelly base, so it fades dark spots without leaving skin tight. Its main job is pigment — the hyaluronic acid is a hydrating bonus, not the star — which makes it a strong fit if your spots come with dryness or a fussy barrier. Use it at night and follow with a moisturizer if your skin runs very dry. La Roche-Posay Mela B3 — ~$45. This serum leads with Melasyl and 10% niacinamide, a gentle combination that fades sun spots, age spots, and post-acne marks while the niacinamide supports the barrier. It's a good middle-of-the-road pick for sensitive skin that can't handle stronger acids, though results are gradual. iS Clinical Hydra-Cool Serum — ~$108. Hydra-Cool is the most hydration-forward option here, built on hyaluronic acid and soothing centella, with kojic acid for a mild brightening assist. Choose it if hydration and calming redness are your priority and dark spots are a secondary concern — it's more of a comfort serum with brightening support than a heavy-duty corrector. SkinCeuticals Discoloration Defense — ~$115. This is the most targeted pigment corrector on the list, combining 3% tranexamic acid, 1% kojic acid, and 5% niacinamide to tackle stubborn brown patches and post-acne marks. It's water-light rather than richly hydrating, so pair it with a hyaluronic acid serum or moisturizer if your skin needs extra moisture. Good Molecules Discoloration Correcting Serum — ~$12. The budget standout, this lightweight serum uses a tranexamic acid derivative plus 4% niacinamide to fade discoloration for a fraction of the price of the premium picks. The thin, water-gel texture layers easily under a hydrating moisturizer, which is the easiest way to make it a "hydrating" step. Prices are approximate and were web-checked on August 12, 2026; they vary by retailer and over time. How do you use a hydrating dark-spot serum? Apply a hydrating dark-spot serum to clean, slightly damp skin once or twice a day, then seal it with a moisturizer and — every morning — sunscreen. Damp skin gives the hyaluronic acid water to grab, and the moisturizer on top locks everything in. If you're new to acids, start every other night and build up as your skin adjusts. Sun protection is not optional here. The American Academy of Dermatology says effective treatment for dark spots "begins with sunscreen," and recommends a broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher, ideally a tinted mineral formula with iron oxide for extra protection against the visible light that can worsen pigment. Without daily SPF, new sun exposure will keep re-darkening the spots you're trying to fade. Frequently Asked Questions How long does it take for dark spots to fade? Most dark spots that are only a few shades darker than your skin fade within 6 to 12 months of consistent treatment, according to the American Academy of Dermatology. Deeper or older discoloration can take longer, sometimes years. Daily sunscreen speeds the process by preventing spots from re-darkening. Can I layer hyaluronic acid with acids or vitamin C? Yes, hyaluronic acid layers well with pigment-fading acids and vitamin C, and it often makes them more comfortable to use. Apply the treatment serum first, then a hyaluronic acid serum or moisturizer to cushion it. Because hyaluronic acid is a humectant rather than an active, it rarely causes conflicts or irritation. Do I still need sunscreen if my serum fades dark spots? Yes — sunscreen is the single most important step when fading dark spots. The American Academy of Dermatology calls it the foundation of treatment, because UV and visible light drive pigment production and will undo a serum's progress. Use a broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher every morning, even indoors near windows. Is a hydrating serum enough for melasma? A hydrating dark-spot serum can help maintain and gradually improve melasma, but stubborn or hormonal melasma often needs a dermatologist's plan, which may include prescription options. Serums with tranexamic acid and azelaic acid are reasonable starting points, and rigorous daily sun protection is essential for any melasma routine. Can dry or sensitive skin use tranexamic acid? Yes, tranexamic acid is one of the better-tolerated dark-spot ingredients for dry and sensitive skin, especially in a hydrating base. It fades pigment without the peeling or stinging that stronger acids and retinoids can cause. If your skin is reactive, start a few times a week and pair it with a fragrance-free moisturizer. The Bottom Line You don't have to trade a hydrated face for a clearer one. The serums that work best for dark spots on dry or sensitive skin combine a gentle, proven pigment-fader with a humectant like hyaluronic acid, so pigment lifts while your barrier stays comfortable — and comfortable skin is skin you'll actually treat every night. If you want that pairing in a single bottle, start with UNSPOTTED 4X Acid Jelly Night Serum for its mix of tranexamic and azelaic acids with hydrating hyaluronic acid, or build your own duo by layering a targeted corrector like SkinCeuticals Discoloration Defense over a hyaluronic acid serum. Whichever route you choose, give it a few months and wear sunscreen every day — that's the part that decides whether your spots actually fade. This article is for general educational purposes and is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. If you have persistent or changing dark spots, melasma, or sensitive skin, consult a board-certified dermatologist.

title: High-Risk Payment Gateway for Shopify: What Merchants Should Consider
summary: Learn what high-risk Shopify merchants should consider when choosing a payment gateway, including fees, reserves, fraud prevention, settlements, and compliance.
body_text: Table of Contents Toggle High-risk Shopify merchants often face more scrutiny when choosing a payment gateway. Approval requirements, reserves, settlement timelines, fraud controls, and supported business categories can vary significantly between providers. This makes gateway selection especially important for merchants operating in categories with higher dispute, fraud, regulatory, or compliance risk. This guide explains the key factors high-risk Shopify merchants should evaluate when choosing a payment gateway, along with how Cashfree approaches payment processing and risk management for eligible businesses. Understand Your Risk Profile Before Choosing a Gateway High-risk classification can result from several factors. Understanding these elements helps merchants identify the payment solutions and requirements that are most relevant to their business. Industry classification is one factor in an initial risk assessment, and certain sectors may receive additional scrutiny because of regulatory requirements, transaction patterns, dispute rates, or consumer protection considerations. These may include: Subscription services with recurring billing Certain digital products and services Nutraceuticals and supplements Financial services and consulting Adult products and content Being in one of these categories does not automatically mean a business will be classified as high-risk. Payment providers generally assess the business model, products or services, transaction profile, geography, processing history, and other factors before determining eligibility and risk requirements. Processing history can also influence risk perception. Previous chargeback rates, processing volumes, refunds , and transaction patterns may affect underwriting decisions. New businesses without an established processing history may face different requirements from established merchants with a longer track record. Business model characteristics can also affect risk assessment. Average transaction size, expected processing volume, customer geography, refund policies, and international transactions may all be considered during onboarding. For Shopify merchants, these factors make it important to check category eligibility and underwriting requirements before choosing a payment gateway. Start Accepting Payments Why High-Risk Merchants Need Stronger Payment Controls High-risk merchants may need more than basic payment processing. Fraud prevention, transaction monitoring, chargeback management, and flexible risk controls can become particularly important when a business operates with elevated payment risk. Fraud Prevention High-risk merchants may face greater exposure to fraudulent transactions , making multi-layer fraud detection, behavioural analysis, configurable rules, and real-time monitoring particularly important for identifying suspicious activity before it results in losses or excessive disputes. Security Strong security measures help protect payment information and reduce exposure to payment-related threats. Encryption, tokenisation , authentication, and appropriate compliance controls form an important part of a payment gateway’s security architecture. Chargeback Management Chargebacks can have a significant impact on high-risk businesses. Chargeback alerts, dispute workflows, evidence management, and transaction monitoring can help merchants respond to disputes more effectively. Flexible Risk Management A merchant’s risk profile can change as its transaction volume, customer base, products, and geographic reach evolve. A payment solution should therefore provide appropriate monitoring and risk controls rather than relying entirely on static rules. The right Shopify payment gateway should balance these controls with a payment experience that does not create unnecessary friction for legitimate customers. Features to Evaluate When Choosing a High-Risk Shopify Payment Gateway Rather than comparing providers only on transaction fees, merchants should evaluate the following factors: What to evaluate Why it matters for high-risk merchants Category eligibility Not every payment provider supports every business model or product category Underwriting process Determines documentation, approval requirements, and onboarding timelines Reserve policy Can affect the amount of working capital available to the business Settlement cycle Determines how quickly processed funds become available Fraud controls Helps identify suspicious transactions and reduce fraud exposure Chargeback support Important when dispute volumes are elevated International payments Relevant for merchants selling to customers outside India Shopify integration Can reduce technical implementation effort Reporting and reconciliation Helps finance teams track transactions, refunds, and settlements Customer support Important when payment interruptions can directly affect revenue Compliance support Helps merchants understand applicable onboarding and payment requirements No single feature determines whether a payment gateway is suitable. Merchants should evaluate these factors together based on their business model and risk profile. The True Cost of High-Risk Payment Processing Transaction fees are only one part of the total cost of payment processing. For high-risk Shopify merchants, reserves, chargeback costs, settlement timelines, and operational overhead can have a significant effect on cash flow. Processing Fees Payment processing fees vary by provider, payment method, merchant profile, transaction volume, and applicable commercial terms. Comparing only the headline rate can therefore give an incomplete picture. A lower transaction fee may not necessarily result in a lower overall cost if the merchant also faces higher reserves, slower settlements, additional chargeback costs, or other operational expenses. Settlement Timing and Reserve Requirements Settlement timelines directly affect working capital. Longer settlement periods can make it harder for merchants to fund inventory, advertising, refunds, and other operating expenses. Some high-risk payment arrangements may also involve rolling or fixed reserves, temporarily locking up part of a merchant’s processing volume. When evaluating a payment gateway, ask: How frequently are settlements made? Are faster settlement options available? Are there additional conditions for accelerated settlement? What reserve percentage applies, if any? How long are reserves held? Under what conditions can the reserve be increased or released? Other Costs The overall cost of processing can also include: Chargeback and dispute-related fees Refund costs Currency conversion costs Compliance or verification expenses Integration and development costs Manual reconciliation and operational overhead Costs associated with processing interruptions Looking at total payment costs rather than MDR alone provides a more realistic basis for comparing payment gateways. Shopify Integration Options for High-Risk Merchants The technical integration method can affect how quickly a merchant gets started and how much flexibility it has over the payment experience. A Shopify app or plugin is generally the simplest integration option where the merchant’s business category and required payment flow are supported. API-based integration may be relevant when a merchant needs custom workflows, specialised transaction handling, subscription billing logic, or integration with other business systems. Merchants using Shopify as a backend while operating a customised storefront may require a headless or SDK-based approach. The right integration depends on the merchant’s storefront architecture, payment requirements, technical resources, and supported gateway capabilities. What to Check Before Integration Before committing to a payment gateway, high-risk Shopify merchants should consider: Category support: Does the gateway support the merchant’s specific products or services? Sandbox environment: Is there a test environment available before going live? Documentation: Are API, webhook, and transaction-status processes clearly documented? Reconciliation: Can transaction, refund, settlement, and order data be matched efficiently? Support: Is technical and payment support available when issues affect live transactions? For high-risk businesses, reliable support can be particularly important because a payment interruption can have a direct impact on revenue and customer experience. India Compliance Considerations for High-Risk Merchants Merchants operating from India should consider regulatory and compliance requirements alongside pricing and technical capabilities. Some important areas to review include: Payment Aggregator framework: Check whether the payment provider is appropriately authorised to provide the relevant payment aggregation services in India . Payment data requirements: Merchants should understand applicable requirements around the storage and processing of payment data. Authentication: Card transactions may be subject to applicable authentication requirements, exemptions, and payment-network rules. KYC and business verification: Merchants should expect to provide relevant business, identity, bank account, and other verification documents during onboarding. Category-specific requirements: Certain products and services may require additional documentation or may be subject to provider-specific eligibility policies. High-risk businesses can face additional underwriting or documentation requirements depending on their category, transaction profile, customer geography, and processing history. Cashfree operates as an RBI-authorised Payment Aggregator and Payment Aggregator-Cross Border provider. Eligible merchants are subject to applicable onboarding, KYC, underwriting, and business-category requirements. How Cashfree Approaches High-Risk Payment Processing For eligible businesses, Cashfree provides payment processing and risk management capabilities designed to support merchants with different transaction profiles and payment requirements. Cashfree’s risk management capabilities are designed to help merchants identify and manage potentially suspicious transactions, while risk controls and monitoring capabilities can form part of a broader fraud prevention strategy. Cashfree also provides Shopify payment gateway integration that allows eligible merchants to connect payment processing with their online store. However, integration availability does not replace the underwriting process. High-risk merchants should confirm category eligibility and applicable onboarding requirements before going live. Payment visibility can help merchants monitor transaction performance, identify unusual patterns, and reconcile payment activity. These capabilities become increasingly important as transaction volumes grow. Settlement requirements and timelines can vary depending on the merchant profile, payment method, risk assessment, and applicable commercial terms, so merchants should confirm the settlement cycle and any conditions that apply to their account during onboarding. A Practical Gateway Selection Framework Before choosing a payment gateway , high-risk Shopify merchants can use the following framework. Step 1: Confirm Eligibility Start by checking whether the payment provider supports: Your product or service category Your target customer geographies Your expected transaction volume Your payment methods Your business model Step 2: Understand Underwriting Ask what documentation is required and whether additional review is needed for your category. Understand the approval process before investing significant time in integration. Step 3: Compare Total Costs Look beyond the headline processing fee and evaluate: Transaction fees Reserves Settlement timelines Chargeback costs Refund costs Currency conversion charges Other applicable fees Step 4: Evaluate Risk Controls Check whether the provider offers appropriate fraud detection, transaction monitoring, chargeback support, and configurable risk controls. Step 5: Check Shopify Compatibility Confirm whether your preferred integration method supports your business requirements and whether the payment flow works correctly with your Shopify setup. Step 6: Review Support Payment processing is a critical part of an ecommerce operation. Evaluate the availability and responsiveness of technical, payment, and merchant support before making a decision. Choose a Payment Gateway Based on Your Business Profile Choosing a payment gateway for a high-risk Shopify store requires looking beyond the headline transaction fee. Category eligibility, underwriting requirements, reserves, settlement timelines, fraud controls, chargeback management, integration options, and compliance support can all affect the actual cost and reliability of payment processing. Cashfree provides payment processing, Shopify integration, and risk management capabilities for eligible businesses. Because high-risk businesses can have different underwriting requirements, merchants should confirm eligibility, pricing, settlement terms, and applicable conditions based on their specific business model. Looking for a Payment Gateway for Your Shopify Store? If you’re evaluating payment gateways for a high-risk or complex business model, Cashfree can help you explore your payment processing options, risk management capabilities, and Shopify integration based on your business requirements. Explore Cashfree for Shopify Frequently Asked Questions What is a high-risk Shopify merchant? A high-risk Shopify merchant is a business that may receive additional scrutiny from payment providers because of factors such as its industry, products, transaction patterns, dispute history, customer geography, or regulatory requirements. Being in a particular industry does not automatically mean a merchant will be classified as high-risk. Can high-risk businesses use Shopify payment gateways? Yes, but eligibility depends on the payment provider, business category, transaction profile, geography, and applicable underwriting requirements. Merchants should confirm category support before integrating a payment gateway. Do high-risk merchants always need a reserve? Not necessarily. Reserve requirements depend on the payment provider, merchant profile, risk assessment, and commercial agreement. Merchants should ask about reserve requirements and release conditions during onboarding. What should high-risk Shopify merchants look for in a payment gateway? Important factors include category eligibility, underwriting requirements, fraud prevention, chargeback management, settlement timelines, reserves, Shopify integration, reporting, compliance, and customer support. Is the lowest payment processing fee always the best option? No. A lower transaction fee may not result in the lowest overall cost if the merchant faces higher reserves, slower settlements, additional dispute costs, or operational limitations. Total cost should be evaluated alongside service capabilities. Does Cashfree support high-risk merchants? Cashfree evaluates businesses based on factors including their business model, category, transaction profile, and applicable requirements. Eligible high-risk businesses can access relevant payment processing and risk management capabilities, subject to onboarding and underwriting.

title: Antes de sacar una tarjeta internacional, hazte estas preguntas - Littio: Tu Cuenta en Dólares y Euros
summary: La app para recibir pagos del exterior, transferir sin fricción, pagar en cualquier país y recibir recompensas en USD* EUR* y COP*.
body_text: Antes de sacar cualquier tarjeta, lee esto Las tarjetas internacionales se anuncian por lo que no cobran. La letra pequeña vive justo en lo que sí cobran, y casi nunca aparece en el aviso. Antes de sacar cualquiera, hazte cinco preguntas concretas: ¿Hay cuota de manejo mensual , aunque no la veas hasta el primer extracto? ¿Qué pasa cuando pagas en una moneda distinta a la que configuraste? ¿Cómo funciona la tasa de conversión y qué margen se esconde ahí? ¿Cuánto cuesta retirar en cajero , dentro y fuera de Colombia? A lo largo del artículo tendremos la Littio Card como ejemplo ilustrativo de cómo se ve un producto transparente en la práctica. ¿Qué es una tarjeta internacional y por qué no es lo mismo que débito o crédito? Una tarjeta internacional multidivisa te deja mantener y pagar en varias monedas desde una misma cuenta, por ejemplo dólares, euros o pesos. Eso la separa de la lógica tradicional que conoces en Colombia. Una tarjeta débito saca fondos de tu cuenta bancaria en el momento. Una tarjeta de crédito te presta un cupo que el banco te factura después La diferencia real de una tarjeta multidivisa no está en si te presta o no plata. Está en qué pasa cuando la moneda de tu compra no coincide con la moneda de tu saldo. Ahí entra la conversión, y ese es el punto exacto donde vive la letra pequeña. El punto de conversión, paso a paso Cada vez que pagas, la transacción sigue un recorrido técnico. La compra se inicia con el tap o la inserción, y viaja por la red de tarjetas (Visa o Mastercard) que conecta al comercio con tu emisor. El emisor verifica tu saldo y autoriza la compra en segundos, según explica Stripe . Antes de que se confirme el cargo, hay una retención que bloquea el monto y baja tu saldo disponible de forma temporal. Cuando la compra involucra otra moneda, la red de tarjetas aplica su tipo de cambio del día antes de que el emisor cierre el cargo. Sobre ese tipo de cambio cada marca puede sumar su propio margen o su propia comisión. Por eso dos tarjetas que corren por la misma red pueden cobrarte cifras distintas por la misma compra. El costo no lo decide solo la red, lo decide lo que el emisor le agrega encima. ¿Dónde queda Littio en todo esto? Littio es una empresa de tecnología que te da acceso a la economía global a través de activos digitales, y opera como mandatario de ejecución para administrarlos y ofrece una Littio Card de Mastercard para que los usuarios conecten sus dólares, euros y pesos digitales con el mundo real, al hacer compras en cualquier parte. La cuota de manejo: la primera pregunta que hay que hacer La cuota de manejo mensual es un cobro fijo que el emisor te descuenta cada mes solo por tener la tarjeta activa, uses o no uses el plástico. Muchas tarjetas la anuncian como algo pequeño o la esconden dentro de un paquete de "beneficios", y tú no la notas hasta que llega el primer extracto y ves un descuento que nadie te explicó al abrir la cuenta. La publicidad se concentra en lo que la tarjeta te ahorra en compras. La cuota mensual queda en la letra pequeña, y sumada durante un año se convierte en un costo real que compite con cualquier ahorro en comisiones. Como ejemplo de cómo se ve una tarjeta sin este cobro, la Littio Card cobra $0 en cuota de manejo mensual y $0 en activación de tarjeta virtual . No es la única en el mercado que funciona así, pero sirve para mostrar que un producto puede vivir sin este cargo fijo. Antes de sacar cualquier tarjeta, hazte una sola pregunta. ¿Esta cuota aparece en la letra pequeña o en el precio que me están anunciando? ¿Qué pasa si pagas en una moneda distinta a la que configuraste? Una tarjeta multidivisa no cubre "todo el mundo" en las mismas condiciones, aunque su publicidad lo sugiera. La diferencia depende de si la moneda de tu compra coincide con la moneda que configuraste en la tarjeta. Cuando la moneda coincide Si tienes tu tarjeta configurada en USD y pagas en USD , la transacción es 1:1 y sin comisión . Compras algo por $10 USD y de tu saldo salen exactamente $10 USD. En Littio Card, ese escenario 1:1 aplica cuando la moneda de la compra coincide con la que configuraste, entre USDC, EURC, COPM o MXNB . Cuando la moneda no coincide El cobro cambia cuando pagas en una moneda que no está en tu lista configurada. Imagina que viajas a Rumania y pagas en RON con tu tarjeta configurada en USDC o EURC. Ahí, Littio Card aplica una comisión del 2% sobre el valor de la compra más la tasa de conversión . No es que la tarjeta deje de funcionar, simplemente te permite usar tus recursos, pero te cobra la conversión y aún así suele ser mejor que las cuentas tradicionales que pueden cobrar desde un 5%. La pregunta que debes hacerte antes de viajar Antes de sacar cualquier tarjeta, revisa qué monedas puedes configurar y qué pasa cuando pagas fuera de esa lista. Littio Card te permite configurar USDC, EURC, COPM y MXNB , y esas son las monedas donde consigues el 1:1. Si vas a un país cuya moneda no está en esa lista, ninguna tarjeta multidivisa te dará condiciones idénticas a las de tu moneda base. La letra pequeña de cualquier producto que evalúes debería decirte con claridad dos cosas: cuáles son las monedas sin comisión y cuánto cobra fuera de ellas . Si esa información no aparece o está enterrada, esa es tu señal de alerta. ¿Cómo funciona realmente la tasa de conversión? Cada vez que compras en una moneda distinta a la de tu saldo, tu tarjeta usa un tipo de cambio de referencia para traducir el precio. Es el valor que la red de tarjetas toma como base ese día para convertir. El detalle importante es el margen adicional que muchas tarjetas suman por encima de ese tipo de referencia. Una tarjeta puede anunciar "$0 en comisión" y aún así cobrarte de más. Ese margen no vive en una comisión con nombre propio. Vive escondido dentro de la tasa de conversión que aplicaron. Por eso, una comisión de $0 no garantiza que estés pagando la conversión más limpia. La pregunta real que le debes hacer a cualquier tarjeta no es solo cuánto cobra de comisión, sino a qué tasa convierte y cuánto se aleja de la referencia del mercado. El costo real de retirar en cajero, dentro y fuera de Colombia Retirar efectivo en un cajero es donde más gente se lleva sorpresas, porque casi nunca hay un solo cobro. Hay dos. Uno lo cobra el emisor de tu tarjeta y otro lo cobra el dueño del cajero, y son entidades distintas que no se ponen de acuerdo entre ellas. Stripe categoriza estas comisiones de cajero fuera de red como un cargo doble por diseño. El operador del cajero cobra su parte, y el banco emisor cobra la suya. Un cajero en el extranjero puede cobrarte lo que quiera por prestarte su máquina, y esa cifra tu emisor no la controla ni la anuncia. Cómo se ve esto en un producto real Littio Card cobra hasta $6.180 COP por transacción al retirar en un cajero en Colombia. Fuera del país, el costo "depende de la entidad propietaria del cajero" , sin cifra fija, porque cada operador pone su propia tarifa. El emisor puede decirte lo que cobra su lado, pero no el del cajero. La pregunta que debes hacer Cuando una tarjeta anuncia un costo de retiro, pregunta si esa cifra es solo el cobro del emisor o si incluye el del dueño del cajero. Casi siempre es solo lo primero. La forma honesta de saber cuánto pagarás de verdad es leer la letra pequeña del emisor y asumir que el cajero sumará su propio cargo encima, sobre todo fuera de Colombia. Apple Pay, Google Pay y otros detalles que sí importan en el día a día No todo lo que afecta tu viaje aparece bajo la palabra "comisión". La compatibilidad con Apple Pay y Google Pay decide si puedes pagar con tu celular cuando la tarjeta física se queda en el hotel o cuando esperas semanas por el plástico. La Littio Card se agrega a ambas billeteras, así que puedes pagar desde el iPhone, el Apple Watch o un dispositivo Android desde el primer momento. El otro detalle es el costo de tener la tarjeta física. La virtual de Littio Card cuesta $0 en activación , pero solicitar la física tiene un cargo de $3 USD . Es una cifra pequeña, y por eso mismo suele quedar enterrada en la letra pequeña del contrato. body_text: Cleva vs LemFi is the question a lot of Nigerians Nigerian in the US ends up asking the moment they need to send money home, whether it’s rent for a parent in Lekki, school fees for a sibling in Enugu, or the monthly “upkeep” alert that lands on the 25th. Whatever the reason, you want your dollars to stretch further in naira, and you want the transfer to land fast and safely. Nigerians abroad sent home close to $20 billion in 2023 alone, and Nigeria accounted for roughly 35 percent of all remittances into Sub-Saharan Africa that year, according to World Bank data . With that much money moving every month, the Cleva vs LemFi decision is not a small one. Below, we compare fees, exchange rates, speed, and the extra perks that quietly save (or cost) you money over time, and explain why Cleva comes out ahead. What is LemFi? LemFi, formerly Lemonade Finance, is a remittance app built by Nigerian founders for sending money from the US, UK, and Canada to Africa and parts of Asia. It’s a popular pick for a US to Nigeria money transfer because it was designed specifically for the diaspora, with zero transfer fees, fast bank deposits, and rates that track close to the parallel market . What is Cleva? Cleva is a Nigerian fintech platform built to be more than a single-purpose transfer app, the biggest structural difference in the Cleva vs LemFi comparison. It gives you a real US dollar account, a virtual dollar card, and a fast way to transfer money from USA to Nigeria, plus diaspora-specific features: paying a loved one’s electricity or mobile data bill directly from the U.S. at a discount, and Pots, a savings feature that earns rewards on money you set aside. For anyone comparing the best remittance apps for Nigerians in USA, Cleva is a full financial home, not just a pipe for moving cash. Cleva vs LemFi: Fees and Exchange Rates This is where most people start their Cleva vs LemFi comparison. LemFi advertises zero transfer fees on many routes including Nigeria, though some transactions to other countries carry a fee, and later transfers to a corridor can attract a charge even when the first one was free . The real cost with LemFi tends to hide in the exchange rate margin rather than an upfront fee, so what your family receives depends on the rate quoted that day. Cleva takes a more transparent route, with no guessing about hidden markups eating into what your loved ones receive. That matters if you’re searching for the cheapest way to send money to Nigeria, because a “zero fee” headline means little if the exchange rate quietly makes up the difference. It’s a core reason Cleva vs LemFi keeps coming up in diaspora finance forums. The table above sums up the Cleva vs LemFi feature gap at a glance. Speed: Can you send money to Nigeria instantly? Nobody wants to send money to Nigeria instantly only to watch it sit “processing” during a family emergency. LemFi’s bank-to-bank transfers on core corridors like Nigeria typically arrive within minutes, though less common routes can take one to two business days . Cleva is built for the same urgency, whether you’re topping up a Cleva Classic Card, moving cash into Pots, or sending straight to a Nigerian bank account. On speed, Cleva vs LemFi is close to a tie, so the real gap sits in what happens after the money lands. Cleva vs LemFi: Rewards and Extra Perks Here’s where Cleva vs LemFi really tips in one direction. LemFi is, at its core, a transfer app that moves money from point A to point B, and that’s largely where it ends. Cleva was built differently. With Cleva, every transfer can earn you Points rewards, so sending money to Nigeria isn’t just an expense, it’s an action that gives something back. Beyond transfers, Cleva lets you pay a loved one’s mobile data bill directly from the US at a 3% discount and cover their electricity bill at a 1% discount, without funneling cash through a middleman first. And with Pots, money you set aside earns 3% rewards instead of sitting idle. None of this exists on LemFi, which is exactly why Cleva vs LemFi isn’t really a close contest once you look past the headline transfer fee. Is Cleva a good LemFi alternative? If you’ve used LemFi purely for cash transfers and want a LemFi alternative that does more, Cleva is worth the switch. You keep the core benefit, a reliable way to transfer money from USA to Nigeria, plus a full USD account, a card usable anywhere Visa or Mastercard is accepted, real bill-payment discounts, and a rewards-earning savings feature. For remittance Nigeria USA use cases where you send regularly, those extras add up fast. How to receive money from USA in Nigeria with Cleva Setup is simple: open a Cleva account, verify your identity, fund your US dollar balance, and send to a Nigerian bank account within minutes. Recipients don’t need a Cleva account to receive a bank transfer, so it’s just as easy for family as any other app. Whether they use a dollar to naira transfer app or handle a USDT to naira transfer for savings, Cleva’s ecosystem supports both under one roof. Cleva vs LemFi: Frequently Asked Questions 1. Is Cleva cheaper than LemFi for sending money to Nigeria? In the Cleva vs LemFi price comparison, it depends on the exchange rate on the day you send, but Cleva’s transparent pricing plus its rewards, discounted bill payments, and Pots savings often make it the better long-term choice, even when both apps look similar on a single transfer. 2. What’s the best way to send money to Nigeria from USA if I send often? If you’re sending regularly rather than once, Cleva is the better way to send money to Nigeria from USA because you build up points rewards, can pay bills at a discount, and can grow idle cash in Pots between transfers, none of which LemFi offers. 3. Is there a way to send money to Nigeria from the U.S. with zero fees? Both apps advertise low or zero fees on standard transfers, so if you’re hunting for how to send money to Nigeria zero fees, compare the live exchange rate on both before you send, since that’s usually where the real cost sits. 4. Can I send money to a naira account from USA directly? Yes. Both apps let you send money to a naira account from USA straight to a Nigerian bank, but only Cleva lets you also fund electricity and data bills for the same recipient, another point in Cleva’s favour in the Cleva vs LemFi matchup. Conclusion The best remittance app treats sending money home as more than a transaction. LemFi covers the basics well, but in the Cleva vs LemFi matchup, Cleva goes further, with a real US dollar account, a virtual card, discounted bill payments for loved ones, and rewards on both transfers and savings. title: Q32 Bio Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Corporate Update
summary: -- Reported positive bempikibart 36-week topline results from Part B of SIGNAL-AA clinical trial; additional details from 36-week results and initial findings from 52-week results to be presented at a medical conference in the second half of 2026 -- -- Patient enrollment and dosing in SIGNAL-AA
body_text: Q32 Bio Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Corporate Update August 5, 2026 PDF Version -- Reported positive bempikibart 36-week topline results from Part B of SIGNAL-AA clinical trial; additional details from 36-week results and initial findings from 52-week results to be presented at a medical conference in the second half of 2026 -- -- Patient enrollment and dosing in SIGNAL-AA Part B open-label extension (OLE) ongoing -- -- Registration-directed program evaluating bempikibart in patients with severe or very severe AA expected to initiate in 1H'2027 subject to planned regulatory discussions later this year -- -- Half-life extended fully human anti-IL-7Rα antibody, ADX-914-XL, advancing in pre-clinical development -- -- Completed $200 million public offering in July 2026 -- -- Cash and cash equivalents of $106.3 million as of June 30, 2026, combined with proceeds from July 2026 public offering, are expected to provide financial runway through Phase 3 topline results from planned registration-directed program -- WALTHAM, Mass. , Aug. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Q32 Bio Inc. (Nasdaq: QTTB) ("Q32 Bio"), a clinical stage biotechnology company focused on developing innovative therapies for alopecia areata ("AA") and other autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, today reported financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and provided recent corporate updates. "Our progress so far this year has been transformative for Q32 Bio and our bempikibart development program. In July, we reported positive topline results from Part B of our SIGNAL-AA program, demonstrating clinically meaningful efficacy, preliminary signs of durability, and a well-tolerated safety profile in patients with severe and very severe alopecia areata. We look forward to sharing additional details from our 36-week results and initial findings from our 52-week results at an upcoming medical meeting," said Jodie Morrison, Chief Executive Officer of Q32 Bio. "The emerging profile of bempikibart represents a compelling opportunity to address the shortcomings of currently available treatments for patients in need of an effective, safe, and more durable alternative. We believe our data has set the bar for a biologic in alopecia areata and demonstrates the potential for bempikibart to become a standard of care, first-line option for patients." Ms. Morrison added, "With our recently completed public offering and 36-week Part B results, we are well positioned to advance planned regulatory discussions and initiate a registration-directed program evaluating bempikibart in severe and very severe alopecia areata in the first half of 2027. Additionally, we believe the results observed across bempikibart development to date represent a foundation for broader development, and we are currently evaluating opportunities in expanded alopecia areata populations, as well as in additional I&I indications where IL-7 and TSLP signaling play a role. In parallel, we are advancing a half-life extended development candidate with the same mechanism of action as bempikibart." Second Quarter 2026 and Recent Business Highlights Reported positive 36-week topline results from Part B of the SIGNAL-AA Phase 2a clinical trial. The Part B portion of the SIGNAL-AA Phase 2a clinical trial is an open-label clinical trial evaluating bempikibart, a fully human anti-IL-7Rα antibody designed to re-regulate adaptive immune function by blocking IL-7 and TSLP signaling, in 33 patients with severe or very severe AA with a maximum duration of current episode of four years. Patients are treated with bempikibart for 36 weeks, with off-drug follow-up out to 52 weeks before optional enrollment in the open-label extension ("OLE"). In Part B, bempikibart demonstrated clinically meaningful efficacy on the primary endpoint with a mean percent reduction in Severity of Alopecia Tool ("SALT") score from baseline of 35.3% in the prespecified modified intent-to-treat ("mITT") analysis. Additionally, 40.0% of patients achieved a SALT-20 (80% of scalp hair coverage) response at Week 36 in the mITT analysis and 30.3% of patients achieved a SALT-20 response at Week 36 in the intent-to-treat ("ITT") analysis of all enrolled patients. In Part B, bempikibart was generally well-tolerated, consistent with prior studies, with no new safety signals, and demonstrated a favorable pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic and anti-drug antibody profile. Results from SIGNAL-AA Part B, including additional Week 36 data as well as initial findings from the off-drug period through Week 52, will be presented at a medical meeting in the second half of 2026. Patient enrollment and dosing in the SIGNAL-AA Part B OLE remain ongoing. Following completion of the Part B 36-week treatment period and 16-week off-drug follow-up period through Week 52, eligible patients can enroll in an OLE. Enrollment and dosing remain ongoing in the OLE. Analysis from the Part B 16-week off-drug follow-up period and OLE will inform the bempikibart long-term chronic maintenance regimen, which could include monthly, bi-monthly or quarterly dosing, which will be evaluated in future studies. Q32 Bio anticipates data from the Part B OLE in the second half of 2027. Registration-directed program evaluating bempikibart in patients with severe or very severe AA expected to initiate in the first half of 2027 and additional development opportunities being evaluated. Q32 Bio plans to advance bempikibart in patients with severe or very severe AA into a registration-directed program in the first half of 2027 subject to planned regulatory discussions in the second half of 2026. Additionally, based on results observed, Q32 Bio is evaluating opportunities for bempikibart in expanded AA populations as well as in additional immunology and inflammation ("I&I") indications. Half-life extended fully human anti-IL-7Rα antibody, ADX-914-XL, advancing in pre-clinical development. Today, Q32 Bio announced that ADX-914-XL, a fully human half-life extended anti-IL-7Rα antibody designed to re-regulate adaptive immune function by blocking IL-7 and TSLP signaling, is advancing in pre-clinical development. Developed using half-life extension technology, ADX-914-XL is designed to provide the clinical activity and safety profile observed to date with bempikibart while offering an extended dosing schedule. Completed $200.0 million public offering. In July 2026, Q32 Bio completed a public offering of common stock and pre-funded warrants, raising gross proceeds of approximately $200.0 million, before deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and offering expenses payable by Q32 Bio. Financial Results Cash and cash equivalents were $106.3 million as of June 30, 2026, which excludes proceeds from our July 2026 public offering. Q32 Bio believes its cash and cash equivalents as of June 30, 2026, combined with proceeds from the July 2026 public offering, are sufficient to fund operations through topline Phase 3 results from its planned registration-directed program evaluating bempikibart in patients with severe or very severe AA. Research and development expenses were $4.3 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $5.2 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The decrease was due to lower ADX-097 spend due to the sale of the program in November 2025, partially offset by higher bempikibart manufacturing costs and nonclinical activities as compared to the prior year. General and administrative expenses were $4.9 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $4.0 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher stock-based compensation expense and other expenses as compared to the prior year. Net loss was $8.9 million, or $0.44 basic and diluted net loss per share, for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to net loss of $9.5 million, or $0.78 basic and diluted net loss per share, for the three months ended June 30, 2025. About Q32 Bio Q32 Bio is a clinical stage biotechnology company whose science targets potent regulators of the adaptive immune system to re-balance immunity and is focused on developing innovative therapies for alopecia areata and other autoimmune and inflammatory diseases. About 700,000 people in the United States live with alopecia areata1, a disease which has a life-altering impact on patients and limited current treatment options. Q32 Bio is advancing bempikibart (ADX-914), a fully human anti-IL-7Rα antibody that re-regulates adaptive immune function, for the treatment of alopecia areata in an ongoing Phase 2 program. The IL-7 and TSLP pathways have been genetically and biologically implicated in driving several T cell-mediated pathological processes in numerous autoimmune diseases. title: Ex-Post Facto Environmental Clearance & Retrospective Regularisation - UPSC Notes
summary: Unpacking the Supreme Court's verdict on retrospective regularisation and why ex-post facto environmental clearance threatens ecological integrity.
body_text: Ex-Post Facto Environmental Clearance & Retrospective Regularisation - UPSC Notes Aug, 2026 • 10 min read Context Fig: The statutory framework under Indian environmental law requires prior ecological assessment to balance industrial expansion with the Precautionary Principle. Ex-post facto environmental clearance undermines statutory regulatory frameworks by permitting industrial projects to initiate construction without prior ecological appraisal. This practice effectively substitutes the mandatory Precautionary Principle under Section 20 of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 with a retrospective monetary penalty regime. According to the Supreme Court judgment in Vanashakti v. Union of India , administrative Office Memorandums cannot override statutory delegated legislation like the Environmental Impact Assessment Notification, 2006. On July 29, 2026, a three-judge Bench quashed the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change's July 7, 2021 Office Memorandum, which had established a Standard Operating Procedure to regularise unapproved projects. This ruling enforces the principle that prior assessment is mandatory under Section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, ensuring that economic development does not bypass statutory environmental safeguards. The Genesis of the Controversy: A Landmark Case of Retrospective Regularisation The Supreme Court of India quashed the administrative framework for retrospective environmental clearances on July 29, 2026, invalidating executive mechanisms that bypassed prior environmental appraisal. In Vanashakti v. Union of India, a three-judge Bench evaluated the legality of executive attempts to regularise non-compliant industrial operations. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) had issued an Office Memorandum on July 7, 2021, establishing a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) to grant ex-post facto environmental clearance (EC) to projects operating without prior appraisal. According to the Supreme Court judgment in Vanashakti v. Union of India, an administrative Office Memorandum cannot supplant delegated legislation like the EIA Notification, 2006 to create a perpetual retrospective clearance framework. The Court quashed the 2021 Office Memorandum with prospective effect, holding that executive instructions cannot dilute statutory rules. However, the Bench clarified two critical legal provisions to maintain balance: Statutory Amnesties: The Central Government retains statutory power under Section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 to frame narrowly tailored amnesty schemes for non-compliant projects under supervening public interest. Plenary Powers: The ruling does not limit the Supreme Court's own plenary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to grant ex-post facto environmental clearance in exceptional cases to do complete justice. Fig: Administrative Office Memorandums attempted to establish parallel retrospective regularisation routes alongside statutory EIA rules. Discuss with Superkalam How do monetary penalties instead of prior environmental appraisal affect developers' decisions? Ask Now What Is Ex-Post Facto Environmental Clearance and How Did We Get Here? The Environment Protection Act, 1986 mandates under Section 3 that designated infrastructure and industrial projects secure prior environmental clearance before initiating construction activities. Under the statutory architecture of the EIA Notification, 2006 (issued under Section 3 of the EPA, 1986), any entity planning a project listed in its schedule must undergo an ex-ante evaluation. Paragraph 7 of the Notification outlines four mandatory stages designed to evaluate ecological risks before land preparation begins: Screening: Determining whether a Project Category 'B' initiative requires an Environmental Impact Assessment report based on spatial scale and site sensitivity. Scoping: Establishing precise Terms of Reference (ToR) for assessing environmental baseline parameters and potential degradation vectors. Public Consultation: Engaging local communities and affected stakeholders through public hearings to gather context-specific ecological concerns. Appraisal: Scrutinising the final assessment report by an Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC) to recommend approval or rejection. Ex-post facto clearance disrupts this sequential framework by allowing proponents to execute construction first and seek regularisation later. Over the last decade, executive relaxations repeatedly institutionalised this workaround: Notification S.O. 804(E) (March 14, 2017): The MoEFCC provided a six-month regularisation window for projects operating without prior clearance. Office Memorandum (July 7, 2021): The Ministry established an open-ended Standard Operating Procedure to process ex-post facto EC applications upon payment of penalty fees. Governance Dimension Statutory Ex-Ante Clearance (EIA 2006) Ex-Post Facto Regularisation Framework Timing of Appraisal Conducted prior to land clearing or construction Conducted after construction or operation has commenced Ecological Strategy Enforces the Precautionary Principle to avert harm Uses damage assessment and monetary compensation Public Participation Mandatory public hearings under Paragraph 7 Structurally ineffective due to completed construction Legal Status Statutory delegated legislation under EPA 1986 Created via executive Office Memorandums The Legal Clash: Defying the Precautionary Principle and Supreme Court Rulings The National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 codifies the Precautionary Principle under Section 20, requiring statutory authorities to anticipate and prevent ecological harm before project execution. The Supreme Court has consistently held that retrospective environmental regularisation directly violates statutory mandates. In Common Cause v. Union of India (2017), the Court ruled that an ex-post facto environmental clearance is anathema to environmental law and inconsistent with Section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. This principle was reaffirmed in Alembic Pharmaceuticals Ltd. v. Rohit Prajapati (2020), where the Court established that retrospective clearance is alien to environmental jurisprudence and contrary to the Precautionary Principle. Fig: The Precautionary Principle under Section 20 of the NGT Act requires prior assessment to prevent irreversible environmental harm. However, legal ambiguity emerged in subsequent judgments, leading to operational friction within regulatory bodies: The Contradictory View: In Pahwa Plastics Pvt. Ltd. v. Dastak NGO (2022), a two-judge Bench held that the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 does not explicitly prohibit ex-post facto clearances for compliant, economically productive industrial units. The 2026 Quashing: The three-judge Bench in Vanashakti v. Union of India (July 2026) resolved this divergence by quashing the 2021 SOP Office Memorandum, ruling that administrative instruments cannot create a perpetual retrospective regularisation mechanism. Discuss with Superkalam How can the government address public interest without enabling retrospective environmental clearances? Ask Now Where the System Breaks: The Dangerous Incentive for Pollute-First, Seek-Permission-Later The Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 amended Section 15 of the Environment Protection Act, 1986, replacing custodial penal sentences with civil monetary penalties. This legislative decriminalisation, combined with administrative regularisation procedures, alters the economic calculations of project developers. According to judicial analysis in Alembic Pharmaceuticals (2020) and Vanashakti (2026), substituting prior clearance with monetary fines generates a severe moral hazard. Project proponents treat environmental penalties merely as a regular cost of doing business, embedding a "pollute first, pay fine later" approach into project development. Fig: Executing construction before securing environmental clearance bypasses screening, scoping, and public consultation stages. Retrospective regularisation fundamentally breaks the four-stage EIA process under Paragraph 7 of the 2006 Notification: Irreversible Baseline Alteration: Soil excavation, hydrology disruption, and tree felling occur before baseline ecological data can be documented, rendering scoping exercises meaningless. Neutralised Public Consultation: Local communities lose the ability to oppose project siting or demand mitigation measures during public hearings when physical structures are already constructed. Compromised EAC Appraisal: Expert Appraisal Committees face fait accompli scenarios, where rejecting clearance would mean ordering the demolition of fully constructed, capital-intensive infrastructure. The Way Forward: Restoring Ex-Ante Integrity in Environmental Governance Rebuilding statutory environmental governance requires the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change to strictly enforce ex-ante appraisals while limiting executive amnesties. To align national industrial expansion with environmental law, reform efforts must focus on three core governance measures: Strict Statutory Compliance: The MoEFCC must restrict clearance procedures to delegated legislation under Section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, abandoning the practice of using administrative Office Memorandums to grant procedural exemptions. Narrowly Tailored Amnesties: As permitted in the Vanashakti ruling, any future regularisation scheme must be framed strictly via statutory rules for exceptional cases involving supervening public interest, rather than functioning as an open-ended SOP. Judicial Restraint and Oversight: The Supreme Court's plenary power under Article 142 should be exercised sparingly to prevent judicial regularisation from becoming an informal alternative to statutory ex-ante appraisals. Key Takeaways Statutory Requirement: Section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 and the EIA Notification, 2006 mandate prior environmental clearance before any site construction begins. Executive SOP Quashed: On July 29, 2026, the Supreme Court quashed the MoEFCC's July 7, 2021 Office Memorandum in Vanashakti v. Union of India, ruling that executive memorandums cannot override statutory rules. Jurisprudential Barrier: In Common Cause (2017) and Alembic Pharmaceuticals (2020), the Supreme Court ruled that ex-post facto clearances violate the Precautionary Principle codified under Section 20 of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010. Systemic Breakdown: Retrospective regularisations turn public hearings and scoping under Paragraph 7 of the EIA Notification into ineffective exercises, encouraging a "pollute first, pay fine later" approach. Limited Exceptions: Central Government retains authority to issue statutory amnesties under Section 3 of the EPA, 1986 in supervening public interest, alongside the Supreme Court's Article 142 plenary powers. Mains Question "Administrative Office Memorandums cannot supplant delegated legislation like the EIA Notification, 2006 to create a perpetual retrospective clearance framework." In light of the Supreme Court judgment in Vanashakti v. Union of India (2026), critically examine how retrospective environmental clearances undermine statutory environmental governance in India. Paragraph 7 of the EIA Notification, 2006 outlines four mandatory stages, beginning with Scoping followed by Screening, Public Consultation, and Appraisal. title: Concorde International Group Announces Receipt of Nasdaq Notification Regarding Minimum Bid Price Deficiency
body_text: SINGAPORE, July 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Concorde International Group Ltd. (Nasdaq: YOOV) (the "Company"), an integrated provider of technology-enabled security solutions, today announced that the Company received a notification letter (the "Notification Letter") from the Listing Qualifications Department of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”), dated July 1, 2026, notifying the Company that it is not in compliance with the minimum bid price requirement set forth in Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) for continued listing on The Nasdaq Capital Market. This press release is issued pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(b), which requires prompt disclosure upon the receipt of a deficiency notification. Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) requires listed securities to maintain a minimum bid price of US$1.00 per share, and Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A) provides that a failure to meet the minimum bid price requirement exists if the deficiency continues for a period of 30 consecutive business days. The Notification Letter does not impact the Company's listing on The Nasdaq Capital Market at this time. In accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), the Company has been provided 180 calendar days, or until December 28, 2026, to regain compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). To regain compliance, the Company's ordinary shares must have a closing bid price of at least US$1.00 for a minimum of 10 consecutive business days. In the event the Company does not regain compliance by December 28, 2026, the Company may be eligible for additional time to regain compliance or may face delisting. The Company's business operations are not affected by the receipt of the Notification Letter. The Company intends to monitor the closing bid price of its ordinary shares and may, if appropriate, consider implementing available options to regain compliance with the minimum bid price requirement under the Nasdaq Listing Rules. About Concorde International Group Concorde International Group Ltd (Nasdaq: YOOV), established in 1997, is a business-model-driven provider of security solutions and services, supported by advanced integrated technology enabling cluster surveillance of properties and assets with 24/7 system availability and real-time response. The Group offers the i-Guarding suite of smart solutions, including the patented i-Facility Sprinter (IFS), a mobile platform operating on its proprietary Cluster® aggregation to deliver one-of-its kind innovative security and facility maintenance services. The IFS is protected by patents in more than 29 jurisdictions worldwide. The Company further integrates its Artificial Intelligence-as-a-Service (AIaaS) capabilities, enabling organisations to deploy advanced AI-driven solutions without significant infrastructure investment. The company's comprehensive offerings transform traditional security models to deliver enhanced operational performance, consistency, scalability, and cost-efficiency across multiple sectors. title: Secured and Governed your AI Agents: Microsoft Entra Agent ID for Dataverse
summary: Microsoft Entra Agent ID and Dataverse agent users offer a new identity foundation.
body_text: Now in public preview: Microsoft Entra Agent ID and Dataverse agent users AI agents are beginning to play a larger role in everyday business processes—from researching prospects and updating records to supporting outreach and follow-up. As organizations explore these possibilities, it is helpful to have a clear and manageable way to understand which agent is taking action and what it is permitted to do. Microsoft Entra Agent ID and Dataverse agent users offer a new identity foundation for these scenarios. Together, they help organizations give each agent a dedicated identity for accessing Dataverse, assign appropriate security roles, and maintain visibility into the agent’s activity. This approach can help teams introduce agent-based experiences thoughtfully, with clearer separation between people, applications, and autonomous agents. What is Microsoft Entra Agent ID? Microsoft Entra Agent ID extends Microsoft Entra with identity constructs designed for AI agents. Instead of treating an agent as an anonymous automation or sharing a generic application identity, an organization can give the agent an individually identifiable, policy-controlled identity with its own permissions and audit trail. How Dataverse agent users complete the model When an agent needs to work with business data in a Dataverse environment, an administrator creates a Dataverse agent user associated with the agent’s Entra identity. The agent user becomes the security principal inside that environment, where it can be assigned dedicated, least-privileged Dataverse security roles. Authenticate the agent: Establish a distinct enterprise identity for the agent. Authorize only what it needs: Assign Dataverse security roles aligned to the agent’s intended tasks. Separate duties: Distinguish agent activity from human users and conventional application integrations. Audit agent actions: Attribute data access and changes to the agent identity. Manage the lifecycle: Apply administrative ownership and governance as the agent is created, updated, or retired. Why this matters Agent identity turns governance into an architectural capability rather than an afterthought. Security teams gain clearer accountability, administrators can enforce least privilege, and makers can build agentic experiences on a foundation designed for enterprise access and compliance. Example: Sales Development Agent Consider a Sales Development Agent that helps a sales organization keep up with a large volume of prospects. The agent can continuously research leads, prepare personalized outreach, follow up, and hand promising leads to sellers. To do that responsibly, it needs access to CRM data—but it should not inherit broad permissions or operate under a shared identity. How the identity-enabled flow works The agent receives an Entra agent identity. The identity establishes the agent as a distinct nonhuman actor that the organization can manage and govern. The Power Platform administrator adds the agent to Dataverse. A Dataverse agent user is created and associated with the Entra agent identity. The Power Platform administrator assigns a purpose-built security role. For example, the role can permit the agent to read and update eligible leads, create activities, and record outreach outcomes—without granting access to unrelated tables or sensitive fields. The agent works within those permissions. It researches assigned leads, evaluates fit, generates or sends approved outreach, follows up, and updates lead status according to the configured sales process. Actions remain attributable. Administrators can distinguish changes made by the agent from those made by a seller or a conventional application user. Get started with the public preview Start in a non-production environment and identify one well-bounded agent scenario. Define the data and operations the agent needs before assigning permissions. Create or enable the agent identity through a supported Microsoft agent creation experience . In the Power Platform admin experience, add the Entra agent identity to the target Dataverse environment as an agent user. Assign a dedicated Dataverse security role that follows least-privilege principles. Test expected and denied operations, and verify that the agent’s actions are visible in your audit and monitoring processes. Document the business owner, security owner, intended purpose, and retirement process for the agent. Preview reminder: Preview capabilities are intended for evaluation and may have restricted functionality. Validate availability, licensing, regional support, and current documentation before adopting the capability for production workloads. Build agents the enterprise can trust The next generation of business applications will include people and agents working side by side. Microsoft Entra Agent ID and Dataverse agent users help make that collaboration secure by design: every agent can have a recognizable identity, only the access its role requires, and an auditable record of its work. Explore the public preview, test a scoped scenario such as sales development, and share your feedback with the Power Platform community. What business process would you entrust to an agent with its own governed identity? To Learn more: Microsoft Entra Agent ID documentation | Microsoft Learn Dataverse Agent User: Create Entra agent users (preview) – Power Platform | Microsoft Learn
